{{Short description|Indian Light Combat Helicopter}} {{pp-extended|small=yes}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2020}} {{Use Indian English|date = February 2019}} {{Infobox aircraft | name = Prachand | image = File:HAL Prachand (ZF 4834).jpg | caption = A HAL Prachand of [[No. 143 Helicopter Unit, IAF]] | type = [[Attack helicopter]] | national_origin = [[India]] | manufacturer = [[Hindustan Aeronautics Limited]] | designer = | design_group = Rotary Wing Research and Design Centre{{cite news |title=Rotary Wing |url=https://hal-india.co.in/Rotary%20Wing/M__326 |access-date=9 October 2021 |agency=Hindustan Aeronautics Limited}} | first_flight = 29 March 2010 | introduction = 3 October 2022{{cite news |title=Indigenously Designed and Developed Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) inducted into Indian Air Force |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1864787 |agency=[[Press Information Bureau]] |publisher=PIB Delhi ( 3 October 2023 )}} | retired = | status = In service
156 on order | primary_user = [[Indian Army]] | more_users = [[Indian Air Force]] | produced = 2017 – present | number_built = 19 (4 TD, 15 LSP){{cite web|url=https://hal-india.co.in/Common/Uploads/DMS/Conferencecall_17052023_presentation.pdf|title=Analyst Meet 17 May 2023|publisher=Hindustan Aeronautics Limited|date=2023-05-17}} | developed_from = [[HAL Dhruv]] | variants = }} The '''HAL Prachand''' ({{Lit|Fierce/Intense}}) is an Indian multi-role light [[attack helicopter]] designed and manufactured by [[Hindustan Aeronautics Limited]] (HAL) under Project ''Light Combat Helicopter'' (LCH).{{Cite web |last=Bhasin |first=Swati |date=2022-10-03 |title='Prachand': 1st made-in-India light combat helicopters |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/prachand-1st-batch-of-light-combat-helicopters-inducted-in-air-force-101664778735925.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316171843/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/prachand-1st-batch-of-light-combat-helicopters-inducted-in-air-force-101664778735925.html |archive-date=2023-03-16 |access-date=2022-10-03 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}} It has been ordered by the [[Indian Air Force]] (IAF) and the [[Indian Army]]'s [[Army Aviation Corps (India)|Aviation Corps]] (AAC). On 3 October 2022, the LCH was formally inducted into the IAF and was officially named "''Prachand''".{{cite web |title=IAF names HAL LCH Helicopter as 'Prachand', Defence Minister Rajnath Singh takes a sortie: WATCH |url=https://zeenews.india.com/aviation/iaf-names-hal-lch-helicopter-as-prachand-defence-minister-rajnath-singh-takes-a-sortie-watch-2517434.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221029030217/https://zeenews.india.com/aviation/iaf-names-hal-lch-helicopter-as-prachand-defence-minister-rajnath-singh-takes-a-sortie-watch-2517434.html |archive-date=29 October 2022 |access-date=3 October 2022 |website=Zee News}} The impetus for the development of the LCH Prachand came in the form of the [[Kargil War]], a conflict fought between India and neighbouring [[Pakistan]] in 1999, which revealed the [[Indian Armed Forces]] lacked a suitable armed [[rotorcraft]] capable of operating unrestricted in the high-altitude theatre.{{cite news |last1=Singh |first1=Suchet Vir |date=3 October 2022 |title=IAF gets indigenous Light Combat Helicopter 'Prachand' after 23-yr journey that began after Kargil |url=https://theprint.in/defence/iaf-inducts-indigenous-light-combat-helicopters-after-a-23-year-journey-which-began-after-kargil/1149811/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014183821/https://theprint.in/defence/iaf-inducts-indigenous-light-combat-helicopters-after-a-23-year-journey-which-began-after-kargil/1149811/ |archive-date=14 October 2022 |access-date=3 October 2022 |publisher=ThePrint}} During 2006, the company announced that it had launched a development programme to produce such a rotorcraft, referred to simply as the LCH or Light Combat Helicopter. Originally, the LCH was anticipated to attain [[initial operating capability]] (IOC) by December 2010. However, development of the type was protracted and subject to several delays, some of which having been attributed to suppliers. The LCH Prachand draws extensively on an earlier indigenous helicopter developed and manufactured by HAL, the [[HAL Dhruv]]; using this rotorcraft as a starting point has been attributed as significantly reducing the cost of the programme.{{cite web |title=HAL Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) |url=https://www.airforce-technology.com/projects/hallghtcombathelicop/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260303092806/https://www.airforce-technology.com/projects/hallghtcombathelicop/ |archive-date= 2026-03-03|access-date=3 October 2022 |website=Airforce Technology |publisher=GlobalData}} ==Development== ===Origins=== [[File:HAL LCH.webm|thumb|HAL Prachand of the [[Indian Air Force]] |alt=]] [[File:Lch.jpg|thumb|LCH model on display at [[ILA Berlin Air Show]] 2008|alt=]] During the late 1990s, [[India]] and neighbouring nation [[Pakistan]] engaged in a brief but intensely-fought conflict commonly known as the [[Kargil War]]. This war, in which various elements of the Indian military were deployed, revealed operational shortcomings and areas for improvement, particularly the requirement for an [[attack helicopter]] that would be suitable for use within the high altitude climates in which some combat operations were fought along the north-western border region.Gady, Franz-Stefan. [https://thediplomat.com/2017/09/india-kicks-off-production-of-light-combat-helicopter/ "India Kicks Off Production of Light Combat Helicopter."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906223522/https://thediplomat.com/2017/09/india-kicks-off-production-of-light-combat-helicopter/|date=6 September 2017}} ''The Diplomat'', 1 September 2017.McKenna, James T. [http://www.rotorandwing.com/2017/08/28/india-oks-light-combat-helicopter-production/ "India OKs Light Combat Helicopter Production."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171002021822/http://www.rotorandwing.com/2017/08/28/india-oks-light-combat-helicopter-production/ |date=2 October 2017}} ''Rotor&Wing'', 28 August 2017. Accordingly, there was considerable interest in not only the acquisition of a suitable contemporary rotorcraft for the task (as well as to replace several aging types in Indian military service, such as the [[Mil Mi-24|Mil Mi 24s]], [[HAL Cheetah|Cheetah]] and [[HAL Chetak|Chetak)]], but for such an aircraft to be domestically developed and manufactured in India as well. During early 2004, Indian aerospace manufacturer [[Hindustan Aeronautics Limited]] (HAL) declared that the company was in the midst of discussions with the Indian armed forces on the prospects for a potential light combat helicopter derivative of the company's existing [[HAL Dhruv|Dhruv]] utility helicopter platform for the requirement.[https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/indian-dawn-193658/ "Indian dawn."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001075235/https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/indian-dawn-193658/ |date=1 October 2017}} ''Flight International'', 8 February 2004. During late 2004, the Indian armed forces decided to curtail plans to order foreign-built attack helicopters in anticipation of a decision to formally select the tentative LCH.[https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/indian-army-slashes-multi-role-helicopter-requiremen-190455/ "Indian army slashes multi-role helicopter requirement."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001075238/https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/indian-army-slashes-multi-role-helicopter-requiremen-190455/ |date=1 October 2017}} ''Flight International'', 23 November 2004. During 2006, HAL publicly announced that it had embarked upon the development of such an attack helicopter, which it referred to as the ''Light Combat Helicopter'' (LCH). During late 2006, the Indian government decided to aid the fledgling programme via the issuing of external finance to support the design phase of the LCH's development, this was done as to aid the attack helicopter in conforming with the established requirements of the [[Indian Army]] and the [[Indian Air Force]]. Accordingly, both HAL and the Indian Armed Forces commenced exploratory efforts towards the conceptualisation of a combat helicopter to perform in this role. {{citation needed|date=April 2013}} Development of the LCH did not progress to schedule. On 21 June 2007, HAL chairman Ashok Baweja announced that and stated that the first prototype LCH was to conduct its [[maiden flight]] during October 2008, and stated that the company was currently "halfway through the design stage".Govindasamy, Siva. [https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/hal-targets-lch-first-flight-in-oct-2008-215093/ "HAL targets LCH first flight in Oct 2008."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001075127/https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/hal-targets-lch-first-flight-in-oct-2008-215093/ |date=1 October 2017}} ''Flight International'', 21 June 2007. During November 2008, the company declared that, while the first flight had been postponed until March 2009, it was still working to secure [[initial operating capability]] (IOC) for the LCH by December 2010, while it was still anticipated that the type would receive its Final Operational Clearance (FOC) during 2011.Govindasamy, Siva. [https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/india-delays-lch-first-flight-to-march-2009-319107/ "India delays LCH first flight to March 2009."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001074646/https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/india-delays-lch-first-flight-to-march-2009-319107/ |date=1 October 2017}} ''Flight International'', 24 November 2008.{{cite web |url=http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2008-11-23/india/27904413_1_lch-light-combat-helicopter-operational-clearance |title=Indigenous attack chopper to fly in March |access-date=6 February 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411224457/http://hal-india.com/Product_Details.aspx?Mkey=54&lKey=&CKey=63 |work=[[The Times of India]] |archive-date=11 April 2016}} During February 2009, Baweja announced another six-month delay to the development timetable, he also attributed some of the setbacks in the programme as having been a result of HAL's suppliers failing to deliver necessary tooling on time.Govindasamy, Siva. [https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/aero-india-light-combat-helicopter-hit-by-six-month-322526/ "AERO INDIA: Light Combat Helicopter hit by six-month delay."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001075047/https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/aero-india-light-combat-helicopter-hit-by-six-month-322526/ |date=1 October 2017}} ''Flight International'', 13 February 2009. ===Prototype and testing=== [[File:The first prototype of HAL Light Combat Helicopter with tandem crew seating took to the skies on April 5, 2010.jpg|thumb|LCH prototype undergoing engine start at HAL on 5 April 2010]] During late January 2010, HAL stated that the LCH had successfully completed initial ground tests and was now ready to fly; the first flight was anticipated to occur during February.Rao, Radhakrishna. [https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/hals-delayed-light-combat-helicopter-to-fly-in-febr-337814/ "HAL's delayed light combat helicopter to fly in February."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001075215/https://www.flightglobal.com/news/articles/hals-delayed-light-combat-helicopter-to-fly-in-febr-337814/ |date=1 October 2017}} ''Flight International'', 29 January 2010. On 4 February 2010, the first LCH prototype completed its first powered ground run.{{cite web |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/india/report_indigenous-attack-copter-ready-for-first-flight_1344742 |title=Indigenous attack copter ready for first flight – India – DNA |publisher=Dnaindia.com |date=8 February 2010 |access-date=21 October 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100404185607/http://www.dnaindia.com/india/report_indigenous-attack-copter-ready-for-first-flight_1344742 |archive-date=4 April 2010}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.mynews.in/News/HAL_to_flight_test_LCH_prototype_next_month_N36065.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120301204753/http://www.mynews.in/News/HAL_to_flight_test_LCH_prototype_next_month_N36065.html|url-status=dead|title=HAL to flight test LCH prototype next month|archive-date=1 March 2012}} On 29 March 2010, the maiden flight of the LCH was conducted by the type's first LCH Technology Demonstrator (TD-1). It flew a 20-minute flight from HAL's Helicopter Complex at [[Bengaluru]], during which the rotorcraft carried out low speed, low altitude checks on the systems on board. Following the completion of the flight, the crew reported that the performance of the helicopter and systems were satisfactory.An extensive test programme, involving a total of four prototypes, was conducted. During the course of these tests, the LCH gained the distinction of being the first attack helicopter to land in [[Siachen]], having repeatedly landed at several high altitude helipads, some of which being as high as {{convert|13,600|to|15,800|ft|m|abbr=off|sp=us}}. .{{cite web |url=http://news.rediff.com/slide-show/2010/mar/31/slide-show-1-indias-attack-helicopter-takes-first-flight.htm#contentTopM |title=India's attack helicopter takes first flight |publisher= Rediff.com News |date=31 March 2010 |access-date=2010-10-21 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110212000854/http://news.rediff.com/slide-show/2010/mar/31/slide-show-1-indias-attack-helicopter-takes-first-flight.htm#contentTopM |archive-date=12 February 2011}}{{cite news |url=http://www.business-standard.com/india/news/india%5Cs-light-combat-copter-makes-first-flight/390258/ |title=India's Light Combat copter makes first flight |newspaper=Business Standard India |publisher=Business-standard.com |date=31 March 2010 |access-date=2010-10-21 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100404022628/http://www.business-standard.com/india/news/india/s-light-combat-copter-makes-first-flight/390258/ |archive-date=4 April 2010|last1=Shukla |first1=Ajai }} On 23 May 2010, following the successful completion of the third test flight of the LCH prototype, it was deemed to have fulfilled the desired parameters, thus enabling further armed tests to proceed. The second LCH prototype (TD-2) differed considerably from its predecessor, as it was fitted with armaments and featured a substantial reduction in weight. It was publicly unveiled at Aero India 2011 in February 2011. Speaking at the event, HAL stated that the program had exceeded the human and payload requirements mandated by the IAF for its development.{{cite news |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2011-07-25/news/29812484_1_light-combat-helicopter-lch-prototype |work=The Times of India |title=India flies second high altitude Light Combat Helicopter prototype |date=n.d. |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411224457/http://hal-india.com/Product_Details.aspx?Mkey=54&lKey=&CKey=63 |archive-date=11 April 2016}}{{cite web |url=http://www.indiastrategic.in/light_combat_helicopter01.htm |title=..:: India Strategic ::.. India flies second LCH |access-date=6 February 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150316232129/http://indiastrategic.in/light_combat_helicopter01.htm |archive-date=16 March 2015}} On 28 June 2011, TD-2 performed its first flight, allowing it to join the test programme.{{cite web |url=http://www.defenceaviation.com/2011/06/indian-light-combat-helicopter-td-2-successfully-tested-by-hal.html |title=Indian Light Combat Helicopter TD-2 successfully tested by HAL |access-date=28 June 2011 |date=28 June 2011 |work=Defence Aviation |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110705053929/http://www.defenceaviation.com/2011/06/indian-light-combat-helicopter-td-2-successfully-tested-by-hal.html |archive-date=5 July 2011}} On 1 July 2012, the LCH began a series of trials near [[Chennai]]; among other elements, the onboard air speed measurement system was evaluated and various component stresses were measured.{{cite web |url=http://defencenews.in/defence-news-internal.asp?get=new&id=1317 |title=LCH Undergoes Sea Level Trials |publisher=Defence News |access-date=6 February 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411224457/http://hal-india.com/Product_Details.aspx?Mkey=54&lKey=&CKey=63 |archive-date=11 April 2016}} Between late June and early July 2012, the second prototype, TD-2, was involved in a series of sea level trials. These trials covered flight performance, the measurement of loads, and the rotorcraft's handling qualities.{{cite web |url=http://www.hal-india.com/MSM/VOL-5_MSM-94.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=26 September 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116061900/http://hal-india.com/MSM/VOL-5_MSM-94.pdf |archive-date=16 January 2013}} [[File:Armed HAL Light Combat Helicopter.jpg|thumb|LCH armed with [[FZ275 LGR]] rockets and [[Mistral (missile)|Mistral]] missile]] During mid-2012, the third LCH prototype, which was claimed to be significantly lighter than either of its predecessors as well as incorporating various other improvements, was reportedly set to be delivered. The third prototype, TD-3, ultimately performed its maiden flight on 12 November 2014 for a duration of 20 minutes.{{cite web |url=http://www.defencenews.in/defence-news-internal.aspx?get=new&id=pJj3ICfDg9U= |title=LCH TD3 makes a maiden flight |publisher=defencenews.in |access-date=6 February 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411224457/http://hal-india.com/Product_Details.aspx?Mkey=54&lKey=&CKey=63 |archive-date=11 April 2016}} Both TD-3 and TD-4 were extensively used during the test programme for the purpose of testing the rotorcraft's mission sensors and weapon systems, which involved a series of live-firing trials. Reportedly, a total of {{INRConvert|126|c|lk=on|year=2014}} had been sanctioned for the development and structural build of the fourth prototype.{{cite web |url=http://www.oneindia.com/india/rotorplus-hal-funded-lch-td-3-undergoes-first-flight-succes-1559566.html |title=rotor plus: hal funded lch fnded td-3 undergoes first flight successfully |publisher=oneindia.com |date=17 November 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141216221108/http://www.oneindia.com/india/rotorplus-hal-funded-lch-td-3-undergoes-first-flight-succes-1559566.html |archive-date=16 December 2014}} During early 2015, a number of cold weather trials involving the third prototype (TD-3) were carried out at [[Leh Air Force Station]] (AFS). During these tests, engine start-up tests (performed using internal batteries after lengthy overnight exposure to the cold climate without special protective measures being applied) proved satisfactory at the temperatures as low as −18 °C at an altitude of {{Convert|4.1|km|ft|abbr=on}}. Several flights were also carried out to assess the rotorcraft's high altitude performance and low speed handling.{{cite web |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2015-03-02/news/59684200_1_light-combat-helicopter-flight-trials-altitude |title=HAL's Light Combat Helicopter undergoes cold weather trials |work=The Economic Times|date=2 March 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411224457/http://hal-india.com/Product_Details.aspx?Mkey=54&lKey=&CKey=63 |archive-date=11 April 2016}} During the course of these tests, the LCH gained the distinction of being the first attack helicopter to land in [[Siachen]], having repeatedly landed at several high altitude helipads, some of which being as high as {{Convert|13600|ft||abbr=on}} to {{Convert|15800|ft||abbr=on}}.{{cite web |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/hal-completes-hot-high-altitude-trials-of-lch-at-leh/article7610924.ece |title=HAL completes hot, high altitude trials of LCH at Leh |first=Ani l|last=Urs |date=3 September 2015 |work=thehindubusinessline.com |access-date=25 July 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170827222142/http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/hal-completes-hot-high-altitude-trials-of-lch-at-leh/article7610924.ece |archive-date=27 August 2017}}{{cite web |url=http://www.oneindia.com/india/lch-becomes-first-attack-helicopter-to-land-at-siachen-1857693.html |title=LCH becomes first attack helicopter to land at Siachen |work=oneindia.com |date=3 September 2015 |access-date=25 July 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818040559/http://www.oneindia.com/india/lch-becomes-first-attack-helicopter-to-land-at-siachen-1857693.html |archive-date=18 August 2016}} During June 2015, the LCH successfully completed hot weather flight trials at [[Jodhpur]], during which the type was exposed to temperatures ranging from 39 to 42 °C. The flight testing reportedly covered 'temperature survey of engine bay and hydraulic system', 'assessment of performance', 'handling qualities and loads' at different 'all up weights', 'low speed handling' and 'height-velocity diagram establishment'.{{cite web |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bengaluru/Light-Combat-Helicopter-completes-hot-weather-flight-trials/articleshow/47828340.cms |title=Light Combat Helicopter completes hot weather flight trials |work=Times of India|date=26 June 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160210135242/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/City/Bengaluru/Light-Combat-Helicopter-completes-hot-weather-flight-trials/articleshow/47828340.cms |archive-date=10 February 2016}} [[File:HAL LCH Camo.jpg|thumb|left|IAF flying LCH at [[Leh]] during [[2020–2022 China–India skirmishes]]]] On 1 December 2015, LCH TD-4 completed its first flight. By March 2016, the LCH had reportedly completed basic performance flight testing and outstation trials, including a number of live-fire tests involving prototype TD-3 firing 70 mm rockets in its weaponized configuration.{{cite web |url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/hals-lch-passes-rocket-trials-will-participate-in-iron-fist-exercise/articleshow/51390574.cms |title=HAL's LCH passes rocket trials; will participate in 'Iron Fist' exercise |website=The Economic Times |date= 14 March 2016 |access-date= 6 April 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160420041945/http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/defence/hals-lch-passes-rocket-trials-will-participate-in-iron-fist-exercise/articleshow/51390574.cms |archive-date=20 April 2016}} By mid-2016, certification firing trials had commenced, these included tests of the integration of its mission sensors, such as the electro-optical system, helmet pointing system, and of the various armaments – [[air-to-air missiles]], turret gun and rockets – that the type can deploy.{{cite web |url=http://www.defensenews.com/story/defense/air-space/strike/2016/05/10/india-conduct-lch-weapons-trials/84175400/ |title=india-conduct-lch-weapons-trials |website=Defense News |date= 10 May 2016 |access-date=21 October 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411224457/http://hal-india.com/Product_Details.aspx?Mkey=54&lKey=&CKey=63 |archive-date=11 April 2016}} During mid-2016, the LCH was recognised as having completed its performance trials, paving way for the certification of its basic configuration; a letter confirming this status had been hand-delivered to HAL by [[CEMILAC]] in the presence of the [[Minister of Defence (India)|Indian Defence Minister]] earlier on16 October 2015..{{cite web |url=http://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/hals-light-combat-helicopter-catches-eyes-of-africas-countries-5-special-facts-about-the-made-in-india-lch/258501/ |title = HAL's Light Combat Helicopter catches eyes of African countries: 5 special facts about the made-in-India LCH |first = Smriti |last = Jain |date = 18 May 2016 |publisher = Financial Express |access-date=27 May 2016 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820190748/http://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/hals-light-combat-helicopter-catches-eyes-of-africas-countries-5-special-facts-about-the-made-in-india-lch/258501/ |archive-date=20 August 2016}} On 31 January 2018, LCH TD-2 was flown with an Automatic Flight Control System (AFCS) designed by HAL. Newly integrated systems include directed [[infrared countermeasures]], Indian-origin [[air-to-ground missiles]] and laser-guided rockets, contemporary [[electronic warfare]] systems, [[nuclear detection]] capabilities, a datalink for secure communication with other Indian military platforms to enhance [[Network-centric warfare|network-centric]] capabilities, and an [[Obstacle Collision Avoidance System|obstacle avoidance system]]. Meanwhile, multiple systems will be upgraded in the serial production helicopters like the [[Electro-optic modulator|electro-optical pod]] for improved tracking, surveillance, and targeting, as well as the helmet-mounted pointing system to improve pilot performance, are among the equipment that will be enhanced. The new systems are expected to be ready by 18 months. The final serial production version will gradually raise the indigenous content from 45% by value to above 65%.{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Rahul |date=2025-09-13 |title=New Prachand LCH to have more firepower, higher survivability |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/new-prachand-lch-to-have-more-firepower-higher-survivability-101757705045687.html |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=[[Hindustan Times]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Shivani |date=2025-09-16 |title=HAL to deliver 156 upgraded indigenous combat helicopters to armed forces by 2033 |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/hal-to-deliver-156-upgraded-indigenous-combat-helicopters-to-armed-forces-by-2033-2788294-2025-09-16 |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=India Today |language=en}} HAL intents to deliver upgraded batches of Prachand from 2027 onwards and complete its orders for 156 choppers to the Indian Armed Forces by 2033. These choppers will be upgraded with [[Infrared countermeasure|Directed Infrared countermeasures]], [[Helmet-mounted display|HMDS]], a new Targeting system, Secure Datalinks,Nuclear detection and [[Electronic warfare]] suites along with newer weapon systems.{{Cite web |last=Sharma |first=Shivani |date=2025-09-16 |title=HAL to deliver 156 upgraded indigenous combat helicopters to armed forces by 2033 |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/hal-to-deliver-156-upgraded-indigenous-combat-helicopters-to-armed-forces-by-2033-2788294-2025-09-16 |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=India Today |language=en}} ==Design== ===Overview === [[File:HAL LCH sortie undertaken by ACM RKS Bhaduria.jpg|thumb|LCH sortie undertaken by [[Air chief marshal (India)|Air Chief Marshal]] [[R. K. S. Bhadauria]]]] The HAL Prachand is a multirole combat helicopter, designed to perform various attack profiles, including relatively high altitude flight.{{cite web |url=http://www.brahmand.com/news/Indias-Light-Combat-Helicopter/3514/1/15.html |title=India's Light Combat Helicopter |work=Brahmand News |access-date=25 July 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819114353/http://www.brahmand.com/news/Indias-Light-Combat-Helicopter/3514/1/15.html |archive-date=19 August 2016}} The design and development of the ''Prachand'' was done in-house, by the Rotary Wing Research and Design Centre (RWR&DC), an internal design office of HAL dedicated to the design of helicopters.{{cite web |url= http://hal-india.co.in/Rotary%20Wing/M__326 |title= Rotary Wing |work= HAL |access-date= 2020-02-10 |archive-date= 28 January 2020 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200128201047/http://www.hal-india.co.in/Rotary%20Wing/M__326 |url-status= dead }} The ''Prachand'' is a derivative of the HAL Dhruv, which had been developed during the 1990s and inducted into the Indian Armed Forces during the early 2000s. Basing the LCH on an existing helicopter is expected to greatly reduce the associated costs of the programme, which was estimated to be roughly {{INRConvert|376|c|1}} in 2010.{{cite web |url=http://www.zeenews.com/news628661.html |title=Indigenous combat chopper takes to skies |publisher=Zeenews.com |date=23 May 2010 |access-date=21 October 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100629152930/http://www.zeenews.com/news628661.html |archive-date=29 June 2010}} Shared elements between the two helicopters include the power-plant used, both being powered by a pair of co-developed HAL/[[Turbomeca]] Shakti-1H1 derived from [[Safran Ardiden]] [[turboshaft]] engines, albeit fitted with infrared suppressors. The features that are unique to the rotorcraft includes its narrow fuselage, a crashworthy [[tricycle landing gear]] arrangement, crashworthy [[self-sealing fuel tank]]s, armour protection, and a low visibility profile; these design elements have been attributed as having resulted in a relatively lethal, agile and survivable rotorcraft. Atypically for a combat helicopter, it shall also be capable of high-altitude warfare (HAW), possessing an in-service operational ceiling of {{convert|6000|-|6500|m|ft}}. Equipped with a two-person [[tandem]] [[cockpit]] to accommodate a pilot and co-pilot/gunner, it has been developed to perform both the [[infantry|anti-infantry]] and [[anti-armour]] missions. In addition to these roles, the LCH is intended to be used for a variety of operational purposes, such as to perform [[air defence]] against slow-moving aerial targets, including both manned aircraft and [[unmanned aerial vehicle]]s (UAVs), participation in [[counter-insurgency]] operations (COIN) and Counter Surface Force Operations (CSFO), the [[Suppression of Enemy Air Defenses|destruction of enemy air defence operations]] and wider offensive use during [[urban warfare]] conditions, escort to special heliborne operations (SHBO), support of [[combat search and rescue]] (CSAR) operations, and armed aerial scouting duties.{{cite web |title=LCH |url=http://www.bharat-rakshak.com/media/4234-3/HAL+LCH+Information.jpg |publisher=bharat-rakshak |access-date=30 June 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140802081918/http://www.bharat-rakshak.com/media/4234-3/HAL%2BLCH%2BInformation.jpg |archive-date=2 August 2014}} In terms of its basic configuration, ''Prachand'' possesses a relatively narrow fuselage and is equipped with stealth profiling, armour protection, and is equipped to conduct day-and-night combat operations. According to reports, the protective measures included in the rotorcraft includes a [[digital camouflage]] system, an [[infrared]] (IR) suppressor fitted to the engine exhaust, and an exterior covered by [[cant (architecture)|cant]]ed flat panels to minimise its [[radar cross-section]] (RCS).{{cite news |title=Indian Light Combat Helicopter TD-2 successfully tested by HAL |url=http://www.defenceaviation.com/2011/06/indian-light-combat-helicopter-td-2-successfully-tested-by-hal.html |access-date=30 July 2012 |newspaper=Defence Aviation |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016231404/http://www.defenceaviation.com/2011/06/indian-light-combat-helicopter-td-2-successfully-tested-by-hal.html |archive-date=16 October 2012}} It is furnished with an integrated dynamic system, including a hingeless main rotor and [[Bearing (mechanical)|bearing]]-less tail rotor, which works in conjunction with an anti-resonance isolation system to dampen vibrations. During Aero India 2011, HAL's Rotary Wing Research & Design Centre informed the press that the helicopter is "probably the most agile design in the world because of its rotor".{{cite news |title=Aero India: HAL showcases new helicopter designs |url=http://www.shephardmedia.com/news/rotorhub/aero-india-hal-showcases-new-helicopter-/ |access-date=31 July 2012 |newspaper=Shephard |date=10 February 2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150220125905/http://www.shephardmedia.com/news/rotorhub/aero-india-hal-showcases-new-helicopter-/ |archive-date=20 February 2015}} In September 2024, HAL assigned TimeTooth Technologies, based in [[Bengaluru]], for indigenisation of Rotor Damp System to be used on HAL Prachand and [[HAL Dhruv|ALH Dhruv]]. The project involves development and qualification of the system for the next two years followed by its production and supply would be for a period of 5 years and beyond. The majority of the project will be funded by the private company itself. The production order value is expected to exceed $5 million within the 5-year period.{{Cite news |last=Dewan |first=Neha |date=2024-09-25 |title=TimeTooth Technologies bags orders from HAL for Light Combat Helicopters |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/sme-sector/timetooth-technologies-bags-orders-from-hal-for-light-combat-helicopters/articleshow/113658911.cms?from=mdr#amp_tf=From%20%251$s&aoh=17273100173643&csi=0&referrer=https://www.google.com&share=https://m.economictimes.com/small-biz/sme-sector/timetooth-technologies-bags-orders-from-hal-for-light-combat-helicopters/articleshow/113658911.cms |access-date=2024-09-26 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} ===Avionics and armaments=== [[File:LCH TD2.jpg|left|thumb|LCH with underwing rocket pods mounted on its stub wings]] The LCH is furnished with a [[glass cockpit]] which accommodates an Integrated Avionics and Display System (IADS) which used an array of multifunction displays in conjunction with the onboard [[target acquisition|target acquisition and designation]] (TADS) system. A prominent element of the TADS system is the [[helmet mounted sight]] (HMS), which serves as the principal instrument for targeting and triggering the rotorcraft's armaments. The LCH is protected via an extensive [[electronic warfare]] suite which is provided by the [[South Africa]]n division of [[Saab Group]]; this suite comprises various defensive elements to guard against several different threats, these include a [[radar warning receiver]] (RWR), [[laser warning receiver]] (LWR) and a [[missile approach warning]] (MAW) system. The LCH is equipped with an integrated [[data link]], which enables the type to participate in [[network-centric operations]] by facilitating the transfer of mission data to other platforms, comprising both airborne and ground-based elements. This networking capable is said to facilitate operational cooperation and [[force multiplication]] practices.{{cite web |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bangalore/Indigenous-combat-copter-takes-to-skies/articleshow/5966664.cms |title=Indigenous combat copter takes to skies |date=24 May 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160411224457/http://hal-india.com/Product_Details.aspx?Mkey=54&lKey=&CKey=63 |work=[[The Times of India]] |archive-date=11 April 2016}} The onboard sensor suite is [[Elbit Systems|Elbit]] CoMPASS, produced locally by [[Bharat Electronics Limited]]. It consists of a [[Charge-coupled device#Color cameras|CCD camera]], a [[forward looking infrared]] (FLIR) imaging sensor, a [[laser rangefinder]] and a [[laser designator]] to facilitate target acquisition under all-weather conditions, including under night-time conditions. The series production variant will come with Integrated Architecture Display System (IADS) and Automatic Flight Control System (AFCS) which are locally developed by HAL with private sector industries.{{cite web|last=Jha|first=Manish Kumar|date=17 November 2021|title=With Certainty, LCA MK 2 Aircraft Is Slated To Enter Production By 2027 And AMCA By 2035--HAL CMD R. Madhavan|url=https://www.businessworld.in/article/With-Certainty-LCA-MK-2-Aircraft-Is-Slated-To-Enter-Production-By-2027-And-AMCA-By-2035-HAL-CMD-R-Madhavan-/17-11-2021-412423|access-date=2021-11-22|website=BW Businessworld|language=en}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025}} During initial development in 2006, it was announced that HAL had selected the [[M621 cannon]] to serve as the gun armament of the helicopter. The M621 cannon is incorporated in a [[Nexter]]-built THL 20 turret and integrated into a [[helmet-mounted sight]]."Missile Mirage", ''[[Aviation Week & Space Technology]]'', 1 January 2007. Various missiles can also be equipped upon the LCH; these include a maximum of four quadpacked anti-tank guided missiles on two hardpoints underneath each wing - options are to include both foreign and Indian-built missiles, the latter in the form of the [[Nag (missile)#HELINA/Dhruvastra|HELINA/Dhruvastra]] anti-tank missile. In terms of [[air-to-air missile]]s, the LCH shall be capable of being armed with the MBDA ATAM missile. The HAL Prachand (lit. 'Fierce/Intense') is an Indian multi-role light attack helicopter designed and manufactured by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) under Project Light Combat Helicopter  (LCH). It has been ordered by the Indian Air Force (IAF) and the Indian Army's Aviation Corps (AAC). On 3 October 2022, the LCH was formally inducted into the IAF and was officially named "Prachand".
The impetus for the development of the LCH Prachand came in the form of the Kargil War, a conflict fought between India and neighbouring Pakistan in 1999, which revealed the Indian Armed Forces lacked a suitable armed rotorcraft capable of operating unrestricted in the high-altitude theatre. During 2006, the company announced that it had launched a development programme to produce such a rotorcraft, referred to simply as the LCH or Light Combat Helicopter. Originally, the LCH was anticipated to attain initial operating capability (IOC) by December 2010. However, development of the type was protracted and subject to several delays, some of which having been attributed to suppliers.
The LCH Prachand draws extensively on an earlier indigenous helicopter developed and manufactured by HAL, the HAL Dhruv; using this rotorcraft as a starting point has been attributed as significantly reducing the cost of the programme.
